issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class Animal and its subclasses: the solution defines Animal(String name, int age) (and subclasses Seal, Pig, Goat mirror this), while the problem statement UML and the template Main instantiate animals with a single String name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This leads to compilation errors for students who follow the UML/template and try to instantiate animals with one argument because the solution requires two.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) remove the 'age' parameter and the corresponding constructor parameter from the solution's Animal and subclass constructors so they accept only String name (and update any code that calls them), or (B) update the problem statement (UML) and the template Main to include 'age: int' as an attribute and change example instantiations to pass both name and age (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", 3)). Apply the chosen change consistently to Animal.java and all subclass constructors and to any example code in Main and the UML in the problem statement.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement/UML declares only a single attribute 'name: String', but the solution's Animal class adds an extra attribute 'age: int'. This divergence is not documented in the problem text or UML and creates confusion about which attributes students must implement and initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the 'age' field from the solution's Animal class so it matches the UML (leaving only 'name'), and adjust constructors accordingly, or update the problem statement/UML to include 'age: int' as an attribute and instruct students to initialize it (and update template Main examples to pass an age). Ensure all artifacts (UML, template code, and solution) reflect the same set of attributes.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the Animal concept: the problem statement and the template Main expect concrete animal constructors that accept a single String name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). The solution repository, however, models Animal with an additional 'age' attribute and defines constructors taking (String name, int age) in Animal and the concrete classes (e.g., public Animal(String name, int age) and public Seal(String name, int age)). Because the same conceptual entity (the animal constructor) has different parameter lists across artifacts, students cannot directly use the example code in Main, will be confused about whether an age is required, and may be blocked from compiling or running the provided template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Animal constructor API across artifacts. Options: (A) Remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and change solution constructors to a single parameter (String name) so they match the problem/template; (B) Update the problem statement and the template Main to require and pass an age (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", 3)) and document the additional attribute; or (C) Add overloaded single-argument constructors in the solution classes (e.g., public Seal(String name) { this(name, 0); }) so the provided Main remains valid while preserving the age-aware constructors. Prefer option C if you want backward compatibility without losing the age attribute.
